approved: Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy Amendment Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that replaces the current Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy with a new industry contribution to fund both the regulatory and financial intelligence functions of AUSTRAC.

The Minister for Justice would set the amount payable by each reporting entity through a legislative instrument, with the total contribution capped at twice the total annual appropriation for AUSTRAC.
Approximately 900 larger reporting entities would pay the new contribution, while about 3,000 smaller ones would no longer be required to pay the levy.
Replace the existing Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy with a new industry contribution.
Fund both AUSTRAC's regulatory and financial intelligence unit functions through the new contribution.
Cap the total industry contribution at twice the annual appropriation for AUSTRAC.
Exempt smaller reporting entities from paying the contribution.
Reporting entities regulated by AUSTRAC, particularly larger ones, and AUSTRAC itself.

Moved the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre Cost Recovery Levy (Collection) Amendment Bill, which shifts AUSTRAC to an industry contribution model covering both its regulatory and financial intelligence functions, and requires an independent review of the levy's operation after the fourth anniversary of the act's commencement.

Reported that the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Human Rights had assessed 11 bills, found 10 did not require further scrutiny, deferred consideration of five and sought further information on the National Security Legislation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2014, including its effects on specified human rights.
